title: Channels
description: Connect an agent to WhatsApp, Slack, Teams, Telegram or email. It answers with the same tools, rules and memory as on every other channel.

connect.title: Connect channel
connect.description: Pick the provider and the agent that will answer. You can start in demo mode and add the credentials later.
connect.agentHint: Answers with its tools, rules and memory.
connect.name: Channel name
connect.localeHint: For the pending-approval and error notices.
connect.demoOn: Nothing is sent to the provider: replies are stored on the conversation and you can test with the simulator.
connect.demoOff: Replies are really sent with the channel's credentials.
connect.templateHint: Template approved in Meta with a '{{1}}' parameter for the text. Optional.
connect.noAgentsBody: Create an agent in the Agents tab to connect it to a channel.

setup.title: Set up “{name}”
setup.description: Finish the connection on the provider with these details.
setup.demoBody: Nothing leaves Messer: use the simulator to chat as a user of the channel. To call the webhook by hand, use the URL with the channel token.

urlLabel.email: Inbound webhook URL for your email provider

secretLabel.demo: Channel token (to call the webhook in demo mode)

setup.secretOnce: Copy it now: it will not be shown again. You can generate another one in Settings.
setup.secretHidden: The secret is only shown when connecting or regenerating it.

whatsapp.1: On developers.facebook.com open your app with the WhatsApp product.
whatsapp.2: In WhatsApp → Configuration, paste the Callback URL and the Verify token, and verify.
whatsapp.4: To answer after 24 hours, create and approve a template and add it in the channel settings.

slack.1: On api.slack.com/apps, enable Event Subscriptions and paste the Request URL.
slack.2: Subscribe the bot to app_mention, message.im and message.channels.
slack.3: Add the app_mentions:read, chat:write, im:history and channels:history scopes and reinstall the app.
slack.4: Invite the bot to the channels where it should answer.

teams.1: In Azure, create an Azure Bot with the Microsoft App ID and its secret.
teams.2: Paste the URL as the Messaging endpoint.
teams.3: Enable the bot's Microsoft Teams channel and install the app in your organization.

telegram.1: Create the bot with @BotFather and copy its token.
telegram.2: Messer registers the webhook when connecting; MESSER_WEB_URL must be a public HTTPS URL.
telegram.3: In groups, the bot answers when it is mentioned or replied to.

email.1: Customers write to the inbound address; replies go out with Reply-To set to that address.
email.2: Point your provider's inbound webhook (Postmark format) to this URL with its token.
email.3: Replies keep the thread with In-Reply-To and References.

setup.sharedEmail: If your provider sends the whole inbound domain to a single webhook, use /api/channels/inbound/email with MESSER_INBOUND_EMAIL_SECRET: it routes by address.

settings.unsupported: This channel is configured from the Voice section.
